title: Probably overpaying, but I built my AI browser game with Lovable
author: JoseQuanGT
selftext:
Im an almost 50 yr old economists from Guatemala… was introduced to Lovable for making dashboards and work apps… ended up building a spaceship/mecha 80s retro arcade inspired by Asteroids and Galaga, that I then converted into a 3rd person forced perspective, used Meshy.ai for 2D to 3D GLB files to crwate 32 image sprite sheets for eaxh enemy type.

Work pays for Lovable, but surely overpaying for what I am getting.

comments.author: ReindeerOk2009
comments.body:
I would export the project and move it over the Claude. That way you don’t have to worry about using works Lovable credits. 

I use Claude for all my 3D models and the bulk of coding tasks related to developing the game. It works really well.

Your game looks awesome by the way!

comments.author: Inhale-aaaand-Exhale
comments.body: Coool game! On the overpaying part..yeah def paying more than necessary with lovable. These days just use Claude like the other commenter said and if you don’t want to do the backend and hosting stuff just plug it into the Floot mcp

comments.author: Pristine_Good7326
comments.body:
This looks awesome! The gameplay and controls feel super smooth.  
Honestly, if you're hitting limits with Lovable, I’d suggest moving your project to a platform built to handle deeper GDDs and more complex game logic. Otherwise, you might end up with results that don't feel much different from what you’d get just prompt-building directly in Claude Code or Codex.  
Lovable is great for getting an MVP out fast, but for something with this much mechanics depth, a dedicated game-oriented tool might save you a lot of headache (and credits)!

replies.author: JoseQuanGT
replies.body:
Thanks Pristine… hope u dont mind that I looked into ur profile and posts, really impressive what u r building… the perfect example of “(skating) **where the puck is going to be, not where it has been.”**

With the advances of AI image generation, bet that in months ur project will run smoothly… a crazy idea of mine is to add dynamic AI gen cutscenes based on the players gameplay (ie combos, chained bonuses, damage taken by what enemy type, enemies killed, pickups, and later type of mission, upgrades earned)… plus the previous games and the game lore context and keep building a story unique to each player.

replies.author: Pristine_Good7326
replies.body: thanks! I love to work on the graphics but the interaction could nvr do as smooth as you lol. Anyways you are already doing a great job! Cant wait to see whats on the plan

comments.author: sw3d
comments.body: Lovable works but Claude Code or Codex is a better bang for your buck. Game looks smooth! Check out my 2D multiplayer version of this genre: spaceships dot gg

replies.author: JoseQuanGT

One question, can Codex or Claude Code host the web game?

Anyways, thanks for the comment and checked out ur game, guess I need much more practice… but very cool, very strong late 1970s Asteroids vibes (which was also my inspiration, only that in mine space and enemies turns around the player, instead of the player turning inside a fixed space)

I also liked the music 😎

replies.author: sw3d
replies.body:
Thank you bro appreciate it :)

Regarding hosting, Codex and Claude cannot do this, they are coding agents without any hosting or deployment built in. However there are a lot of great options for hosting, one of my favorite is Cloudfront which has a great free tier especially if you don't need multiplayer in your game.

If you want the convenience of Lovable with cheaper price for the hosting part, I built homebox.sh which is an open source deployment solution that can let you host the game on your own machine or deploy easily to any cloud platform like Cloudflare, Vercel, AWS and many others 

This is how the spaceships game is currently deployed!
